claim.pdf_says: FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ ANYCASE ] [ FIRST / LAST ] argument-2 argument-3 } ... )  -- printed as ONE tall square bracket enclosing FIRST stacked above LAST (verified at 300 dpi crop), i.e. a single optional choice of at most one of FIRST or LAST; no choice-indicator vertical bars are present inside either the brace or the bracket. FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST are all underlined (required words).
claim.markdown_says:
```
FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ ANYCASE ] [ FIRST ] argument-2 argument-3 } ... )
                                               [ LAST  ]
```
claim.why_it_matters: The one tall stacked-alternatives bracket has been transcribed as TWO independent square brackets, one under the other. Read literally that permits both FIRST and LAST to be specified in the same argument group, which the printed diagram forbids (a bracket around stacked alternatives without choice-indicator bars means AT MOST ONE, 5.2.6.4). The transcription is also the only general format in clause 15 on these pages that uses ad-hoc two-line ASCII brackets instead of the tall-delimiter convention the rest of the file uses (e.g. 15.65.2 MODULE-NAME uses the U+23A7..U+23AD stacked delimiters plus a 'Figure notes' paragraph), and it carries no Figure notes. The required-word underlining on FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST is also dropped, although 15.92.2 on page 955 preserves it.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED after an adversarial pass that ATTEMPTED to refute and failed. I re-rendered page 949 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v949/spec_p949.png) and cropped the 15.87.2 format line at 2x, 3x and 5x (fmt_zoom.png, brace_zoom.png, bracket_zoom2.png).

PDF, glyph by glyph at 5x: underlined FUNCTION, underlined SUBSTITUTE, a tall '(' spanning both text rows, 'argument-1', a tall '{' spanning both rows, a normal-height '[' + underlined ANYCASE + ']', then ONE tall '[' whose top and bottom serifs cross BOTH rows and ONE matching tall ']', enclosing FIRST on the upper row and LAST on the lower row, each word carrying its own underline rule (the middle horizontal rule is FIRST's underline, the bottom rule is LAST's -- they are the width of their words and match the weight of the ANYCASE and FUNCTION underlines). Then 'argument-2  argument-3', a tall '}' spanning both rows, '...', and a tall ')'. I looked specifically for choice-indicator VERTICAL bars: there are NONE anywhere in the figure, not inside the brace and not inside the bracket. So the printed notation is a plain optional bracket around stacked alternatives = at most one of FIRST or LAST, and both LAST and the whole stack sit INSIDE the repeating '{ } ...' brace group because the brace is tall. The claim quotes the PDF accurately.

Markdown, byte-exact (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 38006-38009, dumped with cat -A):
  FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 { [ ANYCASE ] [ FIRST ] argument-2 argument-3 } ... )$
                                                 [ LAST  ]$
Two separate flat ASCII bracket pairs, one per line. The claim quotes the markdown accurately.

MY ATTEMPTED REFUTATION, AND WHY IT FAILS. I first argued this is merely the file's 2-D ASCII idiom for one tall bracket and therefore meaning-preserving, citing 15.68.2 NUMVAL-C (line 37031-37032) and 15.94.2 TEST-NUMVAL-C (line 38363-38364), which render '[ LOCALE [ locale-name-1 ] ]' over '[ argument-2 ]' -- an indisputably at-most-one group (15.68.3 rule 3: 'If neither argument-2 nor the LOCALE keyword is specified...') -- in exactly this flat form. That refutation collapses, because the SAME flat spelling is used in this file for the OPPOSITE meaning: the screen description entry Format 1 clause list at lines 17148-17151 stacks
  [ FULL ]
  [ AUTO ]
  [ SECURE ]
  [ REQUIRED ]
  [ OCCURS integer-5 TIMES ]
on consecutive lines, and those are INDEPENDENT CO-OCCURRING optional clauses -- all may be specified on the same screen item. So flat stacked '[ X ]' / '[ Y ]' does not encode 'at most one' in this file; it is ambiguous between 'choose at most one' and 'each independently optional', and 15.68.2 / 15.94.2 are un-remediated instances of the same defect rather than a convention. Since the flat form cannot carry the distinction, it cannot be a meaning-preserving rendering of a delimiter whose entire semantic content IS that distinction. In a general format the delimiters ARE the grammar, so this is content, not formatting.

WHAT SETTLES IT: THE FILE HAS A DISCRIMINATING CONVENTION AND APPLIES IT TO THE IDENTICAL SIBLING. The transcription reserves the tall U+23A1..U+23A6 delimiters for optional at-most-one stacks -- '⎡ HIGHLIGHT ⎤' / '⎣ LOWLIGHT ⎦' in the screen attribute clauses (line ~17170). And nine sections later in this very clause, 15.96.2 FUNCTION TRIM (lines 38498-38505) is the structurally IDENTICAL construct -- an optional stacked pair of underlined required words inside a function's argument parentheses -- and it is transcribed as '⎡ LEADING ⎤' / '⎣ TRAILING ⎦' inside tall '⎛ ⎜ ⎝' argument parentheses, followed by '> **Figure notes.** No choice indicators in this format. The `[ LEADING | TRAILING ]` group is a plain bracket -- zero or one may be specified. Underlined required words: FUNCTION, TRIM, LEADING, TRAILING.' 15.65.2 MODULE-NAME (lines 36848-36856) does the same with braces. 15.87.2 SUBSTITUTE does neither: it uses the ambiguous flat form AND carries no Figure notes, so nothing in the file records that FIRST and LAST are mutually exclusive. A reader of 15.96.2 correctly learns TRIM's constraint; a reader of 15.87.2 cannot learn SUBSTITUTE's.

SECONDARY LOSSES INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED. (a) The continuation line '                                               [ LAST  ]' terminates after the bracket -- the '}', the '...' and the closing ')' appear only on line 1 -- so LAST is not shown as being inside the repeating brace group, which the tall printed '{' and '}' unambiguously show it to be. (b) There is neither <u> markup nor a Figure notes paragraph, so the required-word underlining on FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST is dropped with nothing recording it; the file's remediated formats preserve it either inline (15.92.2 line 38257: '<u>FUNCTION</u> <u>TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME</u>') or in Figure notes (15.96.2). Neither 15.87.3 nor 15.87.4 repairs the loss: returned-value rule 3 says 'If FIRST is specified ... b) If LAST is specified', which presumes but never states mutual exclusivity, leaving the general format as the sole syntactic authority.

ONE SUB-CLAIM CORRECTED (does not affect the verdict). 'The only general format in clause 15 on these pages that uses ad-hoc two-line ASCII brackets' is FALSE as stated. I found the identical ad-hoc flat rendering of an at-most-one stack at 15.68.2 NUMVAL-C (lines 37031-37032) and 15.94.2 TEST-NUMVAL-C (lines 38363-38364), plus the NUMVAL/NUMVAL-C argument figures at lines 36965-36977 and 37054-37057 which stack '[ + ]' / '[ - ]' and '[ + ]' / '[ - ]' / '[ CR ]' / '[ DB ]' the same way. These are sibling instances of the same defect class and belong in the same sweep, not counterexamples. Also, absence of a Figure notes paragraph is by itself an editorial gap rather than a PDF/markdown content difference (Figure notes are this project's annotation mechanism, present on 225 of 306 general formats, not text printed in the standard); it matters here only because it is the file's designated place to record the constraint the flat delimiters fail to carry.
verdict.corrected_description:
REAL, structural, essentially as described, with one sub-claim corrected and a sweep obligation added.

CORE FINDING (stands, independently re-verified). PDF page 949 section 15.87.2 prints ONE tall square bracket whose serifs span both text rows, enclosing FIRST stacked above LAST, both underlined, with NO choice-indicator vertical bars anywhere in the figure -- neither in the '{ }' brace nor in the bracket -- i.e. a plain optional bracket around stacked alternatives, at most one selectable (ISO 5.2.6.4). The tall '{' '}' and '(' ')' also span both rows, so LAST is inside the repeating brace group. specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 38006-38009 transcribe this as two flat ASCII bracket pairs '[ FIRST ]' / '[ LAST  ]' on consecutive lines, with the continuation line ending after the bracket so that LAST falls outside the '}', the '...' and the ')'.

WHY IT IS A MEANING CHANGE (strengthened -- the proof is internal to the transcription, not merely an appeal to ISO 5.2.6.4). This file uses flat stacked '[ X ]' / '[ Y ]' brackets for INDEPENDENT CO-OCCURRING optional clauses -- '[ FULL ]' / '[ AUTO ]' / '[ SECURE ]' / '[ REQUIRED ]' / '[ OCCURS integer-5 TIMES ]' in the screen description entry Format 1 clause list, lines 17148-17151 -- and reserves the tall U+23A1..U+23A6 delimiters for optional at-most-one alternatives ('⎡ HIGHLIGHT ⎤' / '⎣ LOWLIGHT ⎦', line ~17170). The decisive control is 15.96.2 FUNCTION TRIM at lines 38498-38505, the structurally identical construct nine sections later, transcribed '⎡ LEADING ⎤' / '⎣ TRAILING ⎦' with a Figure notes paragraph stating 'No choice indicators in this format. The [ LEADING | TRAILING ] group is a plain bracket -- zero or one may be specified. Underlined required words: FUNCTION, TRIM, LEADING, TRAILING.' So the flat form at 15.87.2 does not under-render the bracket, it renders a constraint the file elsewhere spells as its opposite, and nothing in 15.87.2 records the mutual exclusivity. 15.87.3/15.87.4 do not repair it (returned-value rule 3 presumes but never states it).

SUB-CLAIM CORRECTED. 'The only general format in clause 15 on these pages that uses ad-hoc two-line ASCII brackets' is false. The same ad-hoc flat rendering of an at-most-one stack occurs at 15.68.2 NUMVAL-C (lines 37031-37032, '[ LOCALE [ locale-name-1 ] ]' over '[ argument-2 ]'; 15.68.3 rule 3 confirms these are alternatives) and 15.94.2 TEST-NUMVAL-C (lines 38363-38364), and in the NUMVAL/NUMVAL-C argument figures at lines 36965-36977 and 37054-37057. Also, a missing Figure notes paragraph is not by itself a PDF/markdown content difference -- Figure notes are this project's annotation mechanism (225 of 306 general formats), not printed text; it matters here only as the designated place to record what the flat delimiters cannot carry.

FIX. Restyle 15.87.2 in the file's tall-delimiter convention so the FIRST/LAST bracket is unambiguously one optional at-most-one group and LAST sits inside the brace group, e.g.
                     ⎧              ⎡ FIRST ⎤                        ⎫
  FUNCTION SUBSTITUTE ( argument-1 ⎨ [ ANYCASE ] ⎢       ⎥ argument-2 argument-3 ⎬ ... )
                     ⎩              ⎣ LAST  ⎦                        ⎭
and add a Figure notes paragraph recording: no choice indicators appear in this format; the FIRST/LAST group is a plain bracket (zero or one may be specified); the braces enclose the repeating group and the ellipsis denotes its repetition; FUNCTION, SUBSTITUTE, ANYCASE, FIRST and LAST are underlined required words in the printed standard. SWEEP the same defect class at 15.68.2 (lines 37031-37032), 15.94.2 (lines 38363-38364), and the NUMVAL argument figures at lines 36965-36977 and 37054-37057.
